chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from al-Marzuban, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his wife, 'Observe your waiting period, for I have released you,' then he testified to her return (raj'a) after that by a few days, then he was absent from her before he had intercourse with her, until several months passed after the waiting period or more. He asked, 'How do you order him?' He (AS) said, 'If he testifies to his return, she is his wife.'
ai.seo_question: Does a husband's testimony of returning his wife in a revocable divorce validate the marriage even if he delays intercourse?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the legal sufficiency of the husband's testimony (shahada) for revocable divorce (raj'a) is established, even if physical consummation is delayed for months. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the marital bond remains intact through the husband's unilateral declaration during the waiting period (iddah), emphasizing the primacy of verbal intent over immediate physical act in this specific context.
